podcast.title: Kurt Cobain's Death Revelation (1994)
podcast.body: On April 8, 1994, during his first meeting with Shirley Manson and other future Garbage members in London, Butch Vig received news that Kurt Cobain had killed himself. This tragic event, particularly significant given Vig's role in producing "Nevermind," caused the nascent Garbage project to be put on hold temporarily. "They all met up in London on April 8th of 1994. Yeah, that's that's right. They met for the first time the day Kurt Cobain killed himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Musical & Academic Background – Wisconsin Roots
podcast.body: Butch Vig grew up in Verlacua, Wisconsin. He took piano lessons as a child and later picked up the drums as a teenager. His academic path included two years in pre-med at the University of Wisconsin, followed by four semesters of electronic music theory, before he decided to drop out and pursue music. "Butch is originally from Verlacua, Wisconsin He took piano lessons as a kid but took up drums when he was a teenager After two years and pre-med at the University of Wisconsin He took four semesters of electronic music theory."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Production Credits – Nineties Music Influence
podcast.body: Beyond his seminal work with Nirvana, Butch Vig produced and remixed records for a wide array of prominent nineties artists. His production catalog includes Sonic Youth, Depeche Mode, Solar Sound, Smashing Pumpkins, U2, and L7. "Butch also produced a remix records for Who's Who of Nidhi's Music Sonic Youth, Depeche Mode, Solar Sound, Smashing Pumpkins, U2, L7."

podcast.title: Producer for Nevermind
podcast.body: Butch Vig, described as a "Madison, Wisconsin-based Sonic Craftsman," produced Nirvana's "Nevermind." He was responsible for achieving a sound that was both "raw and sleek" for the album's recordings. "producer Bouch Vig, a Madison, Wisconsin-based Sonic Craftsman who made his recordings sound both raw and sleek."

podcast.body: Butch Vig is a renowned record producer who worked with Kim Gordon and Sonic Youth on their album "Goo" and famously produced Nirvana's seminal album "Nevermind." podcast.body: At age 36, Butch Vig was asked to produce Nirvana's *Nevermind* album, a project that "set him up for life" due to its monumental success. "before he was asked to produce Never Mind for Nirvana. That's set him up for life, starting age 36."

podcast.title: Shaping the Grunge Revolution – Nirvana's "Nevermind"
podcast.body: Butch Vig's production work on Killdozer's 1989 record "For Ladies Only" attracted attention across the US. This led Kurt Cobain to relocate Nirvana to Vig's Wisconsin studios to work on demos for their major label debut, which later became the album "Nevermind." Kurt Cobain was so impressed that he asked Vig to produce the entire album, a project that helped shape the "whole grunge revolution of the early 1990s." "Kurt Cobain decided to relocate Nirvana To butch's studios in Wisconsin to work on demos for what would become their major label debut."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transition to Producer – Madison Indie Scene
podcast.body: After playing in bands like Spooner (three albums) and Firetown (one album), Butch Vig developed a keen interest in producing music. He established a small studio space in Madison, Wisconsin, where he began working with local indie groups, including Killdozer. "It was around this time that butch became interested in producing music So he ran into small space in Madison, Wisconsin Where he began working with local indie groups including a group called Killdozer."

xref.title: Formation and Search for a Singer
xref.body: Garbage was formed by producers Butch Vig, Duke Erikson, and sound engineer Steve Marker, who specifically sought a female singer in the vein of Chrissie Hynde or Patty Smith, one who could sing in a lower register. "She was drafted into Garbage by three dudes, butch vig, the record producer, Duke Erickson, and another producer and sound engineer named Steve Marker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mastering by Andy Wallace
xref.body: Andy Wallace was the mastering engineer for Nirvana's *Nevermind* album. He applied a "sharp sheen" to the album by extending the high frequencies in the two-track mix provided by the band and producer Butch Vig. This process was crucial for helping the songs "cut through" and made them sound less muffled compared to the studio mix. "He extended the high frequencies to the two track mix, supplied by the band and producer Boots of Vig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mastering of "Nevermind"
xref.body: Nirvana's "Nevermind" album, produced by Butch Vig, initially had a raw punk rock sound that the band found difficult to mix. Kurt Cobain chose Andy Wallace, known for his work with Slayer, to master the record, who added a sparkly edge to guitars, brought vocals forward, and made drums bigger. A final mastering pass was done by Howie Weinberg in Hollywood. The band famously disliked the final master as "too slick" but approved its release. "Kurt Cobain picked a guy named Andy Wallace, who at the time was well known for the sound he was able to get from Slayer."

xref.title: Record Deal Secured by Reputation
xref.body: Garbage sent out samples to record labels with minimal information attached, relying heavily on Butch Vig's established reputation for producing successful albums. This strategy proved effective, as labels agreed to listen and the band ultimately secured a record deal. "Garbage set out samples to record labels with almost no information attached. The only thing anybody knew was that butch vig was involved."
